answer: Each agent must re-solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle every epoch, like a cipher frozen in a glacier that only thaws with real RAM and time. One honest agent pays this once per epoch, but an attacker running a grove of a thousand fake identities must buy a thousand times the memory and electricity, since memory-hard work can't be cheaply parallelized on GPUs. Rewards per identity are set below that cost, so faking agents loses money.
